blocks.text: 1. Context Recall

blocks.alt: A ground truth answer is checked for being covered by retrieved context

blocks.text: Context Precision closed by weighing when its ordering measurement is worth tracking. Context Recall, whether the retrieved context covers everything a ground truth answer actually needed, completes the precision and recall pair applied specifically to context quality.
It checks each fact in a known correct answer against whether the retrieved context actually supports it.
2. Recall At K Versus Context Recall

blocks.alt: Recall at K is chunk-level while context recall is answer-level

blocks.text: Recall At K measures coverage of a labeled set of relevant chunks.
Context recall instead measures coverage relative to a known correct answer's actual content.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","What coverage is measured against"],"rows":[["Recall at K","A labeled set of relevant chunks"],["Context recall","The content of a known correct answer"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Ground Truth Answers As The Yardstick

blocks.alt: A ground truth answer serves as the yardstick for measurement

blocks.text: Similar to breaking the answer into individual claims in Faithfulness, a ground truth answer is broken into its own individual factual statements first.
Each statement is then checked against whether the retrieved context actually contains it.
4. Context Recall Score Is A Fraction

blocks.alt: Covered facts form a fraction of ground truth facts

blocks.text: As with the faithfulness score, the context recall score is the fraction of ground truth statements actually supported by the retrieved context.
It is the same fraction based scoring pattern, applied here to ground truth coverage instead of claim grounding.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A ground truth answer with four factual statements, three of which are supported by the retrieved context, scores a context recall of 0.75, the same fraction based pattern used for the faithfulness score.

blocks.text: 5. Low Context Recall Explains A Low Faithfulness Score

blocks.alt: Low context recall explains a low faithfulness score

blocks.text: A generation model cannot faithfully state a fact the retrieved context never actually contained.
A faithfulness failure often traces directly back to a context recall failure upstream.
6. Context Recall Requires A Ground Truth Dataset
Just as Context Precision needs relevance labels, computing context recall requires a labeled set of known correct answers to check against.
It is a real upfront investment in building that ground truth evaluation dataset.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","What labeling is required"],"rows":[["Context precision","Which retrieved chunks are relevant"],["Context recall","A full ground truth correct answer per query"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Context Recall Pairs With Context Precision

blocks.alt: Context recall pairs with context precision

blocks.text: As with the precision recall tradeoff covered in Recall At K, context precision measures ordering quality while context recall measures coverage completeness.
They are two retrieval-focused metrics answering different questions about the same retrieved context.
8. Raising K Improves Context Recall Like Any Other Recall
Just as increasing K almost always raises recall in Recall At K, retrieving more chunks can only help context recall, never hurt it.
It is the same monotonic relationship, inherited directly here.
9. Recognizing When Context Recall Is Worth Measuring Directly

blocks.alt: Needing to check ground truth coverage points toward measuring context recall

blocks.text: Diagnosing whether a low faithfulness score traces back to retrieval needs context recall.
A system with no ground truth dataset available, by contrast, cannot compute context recall without building one first.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates decomposing a ground truth answer into statements and scoring context recall against retrieved context.

code.content:
retrieved_context = "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month. It includes ten projects."

ground_truth_statements = [
    "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.",
    "The Falcon plan includes ten projects.",
    "The Falcon plan has a thirty day money back guarantee.",
]

def is_supported(statement, context):
    # checks whether a statement's key terms appear in the context
    key_terms = [term for term in statement.lower().split() if len(term) > 4]
    matches = sum(1 for term in key_terms if term in context.lower())
    return matches >= 2

def context_recall(statements, context):
    # the fraction of ground truth statements supported
    supported = [s for s in statements if is_supported(s, context)]
    return len(supported) / len(statements), supported

score, supported = context_recall(ground_truth_statements, retrieved_context)

print("Context recall check:")
for statement in ground_truth_statements:
    status = "covered" if statement in supported else "missing"
    print(f"  [{status}] {statement}")

print(f"\nContext recall score: {score:.2f}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the money back guarantee statement scoring missing since nothing in the retrieved context supports it, revealing a retrieval gap rather than a generation problem.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Confusing context recall with recall at K, which checks a labeled chunk set rather than a ground truth answer.
Diagnosing a low faithfulness score as a generation problem without first checking context recall.
Attempting to compute context recall without a real ground truth evaluation dataset in place.
Ignoring that raising K to improve context recall follows the same tradeoffs already covered for recall at K.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Context recall measures whether retrieved context covers everything a ground truth answer needed.
Unlike recall at K, it measures coverage against a known correct answer, not a labeled chunk set.
A ground truth answer is decomposed into individual factual statements, each checked against context.
The context recall score is the fraction of ground truth statements the retrieved context supports.
A generation model cannot faithfully state a fact the context never contained; low recall causes low faithfulness.
Computing context recall requires a labeled ground truth dataset, a real upfront cost.
Context precision measures ordering; context recall measures coverage, two different questions.
Retrieving more chunks can only help context recall, never hurt it, the same monotonic property as recall at K.
